constraints.pipeline: Existing 768 preprocessing; Telea, LaMa, HINT, Stable Diffusion unchanged
constraints.coverage_denominator: un-padded processed image content; frame/background pixels in source are not cropped
constraints.coverage_interpretation: selected visible repair targets, not an exhaustive estimate of all physical damage

interpretation: Masks are selected digital repair targets on photographs of physical damage, not exhaustive condition maps or clean-reference ground truth. Residual unselected damage is a scope choice, not measured model failure.
cohort_note: Purposive ten-case external-condition study; category labels are operational. Painted wall panels and texture-focused figurative works must be described explicitly. This is not a balanced estimate of all real-world damage.

items.title: Portrait of Antonio van Diemen
items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending
items.note: Visible vertical losses across the background, hat and clothing. Review mask targets clear losses; it is not exhaustive condition mapping. The broader uniform loss on the hat has been included.

items.title: Antigone condemned to death by Creon — before restoration
items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending
items.note: Visible flaking across the left background, cliff and soldier. Expanded after user review to include the breastplate and branching cliff losses. Intact skin, metal, architecture and spear are excluded where distinguishable. No dilation or damage synthesis.

items.title: Horse pasture in Algeria
items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending
items.note: Large open tear on the right and smaller open losses at the left edge. Broader surface abrasion is present outside the selected repair targets; this mask is not a claim that all physical damage occupies only 7.21%.

items.title: Garden fresco, House of the Golden Bracelet
items.artist: Roman, second quarter of 1st century AD; Pompeii, salone 32
items.note: Visible neutral-filled lacunae interrupt the blue sky and foliage. Targets are missing painted content within the panel; ornamental heads, birds and painted pale surfaces are excluded. This is a painted garden, rather than an oil landscape. Photo: Tyler Bell; CC BY 2.0.
items.category_reason: Nature-dominated composition: dense plants, birds and sky; garden statuary is secondary.
items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending

items.title: Landscape with maritime villa
items.artist: Roman; Villa San Marco, Stabiae; museum inventory 62518
items.note: Selected fracture network and an exposed loss at a crack junction. Pale architecture is preserved. Some abrasion and fine cracks remain outside the repair target. Photograph: BeakheadIntrados; CC BY-SA 4.0.
items.category_reason: Built structures and long architectural edges dominate the scene.
items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending

items.title: Cubiculum wall, Villa of P. Fannius Synistor
items.artist: Roman, ca. 50–40 BCE; Metropolitan Museum of Art, 03.14.4
items.note: Selected lower central neutral infill/lacuna. Historical photographs show loss in this lower dado, and the museum conservation report describes fills and retouching. This is not untreated fresh damage: the target lacks depicted content, while other repaired or abraded areas remain. Source: The Met, CC0.
items.category_reason: Architectural perspective, pilasters and repeated building geometry.

items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending

items.title: Watermelon Regatta — damaged state
items.artist: Master of the Fertility of the Egg, early 1700s; The Ringling
items.note: Selected exposed-ground losses near the upper edge plus a visibly worn vertical zone. Not a complete condition map. The category is fantastical imagery, not a claim that this 18th-century work belongs to historical Surrealism. Coverage is close to 2%; the user accepted this scope in visual review.
items.category_reason: Fantastical creatures and deliberately impossible events; operational abstraction/surrealism category.

items.title: Tarquinius and Lucretia — damaged state
items.note: Visible tear lines and flaking cross the drapery, figures and background. Bright painted folds and skin highlights have exclusions. Texture-focused figurative example: the category refers to the rendering of fabrics and painterly surfaces, not to the damage itself.
items.category_reason: Richly worked drapery and painterly figure rendering; a texture-focused figurative case, not an impasto benchmark.
items.status: User-approved source and target scope; notebook validation pending

items.title: Nude — before restoration
items.artist: Hidaka Yasunori; painting subsequently conserved and held at Mugonkan
items.note: Clearly visible light paint-loss flakes around the figure and background. Selected flakes are masked; overall surface deterioration and photographic grain remain. A painterly figurative case, not a claim that scan grain is paint texture. The source PNG has a fully opaque alpha channel: RGB conversion drops only that channel before the unchanged preprocessing.
items.category_reason: Loose, visibly worked tonal modelling of figure and background. Category placement is more subjective than for a pure impasto painting.
